_terms: polaroids.html — what we ask for, what we promise, and how a photo comes down again.
_licence: Photographs here are NOT under the site's CC BY-SA 4.0 licence and carry no onward licence at all. They belong to the people in them and to whoever took them. This is deliberate: CC BY-SA cannot be revoked, so a photo published under it could not be taken back after somebody withdrew consent, and 'it comes down when you say so' would be a promise the licence contradicted. See LICENSE.
_consent: Record only that consent exists and when. Do NOT put anybody's email, message, or contact details in this file — it is a public repository. The conversation stays wherever it happened. To withdraw: delete the entry, delete the file in photos/, and run tools/make-polaroids.py. The wall returns to grey on its own.
_young: Young people who are doing the work and have said yes THEMSELVES are published and credited like anybody else — a lot of Stimpunks volunteers and self-advocates are teenagers, and keeping them off the page hands the credit for their own activities to the adults beside them. The consent has to be theirs: a parent can be in the conversation, but an adult’s yes is not a substitute for the young person’s. Withdrawal works for them exactly as it does for everybody — say so once, and it is deletion. Where somebody is too young to give that consent themselves, we do not publish the photograph and a parent cannot give it for them. Superseded the flat no-children rule on 2026-09-21, Ryan’s call; see DECISIONS.md.
_required: Every photo needs id, alt, subject and consent_on. 'caption' and 'photographer' are optional, but a named photographer must also have given permission — being in a picture is not the same as owning it.
_elsewhere: A photograph may hang somewhere other than Enid's wall. List every other page it appears on in that entry's 'elsewhere' array; make-polaroids.py walks all the HTML and refuses if a page publishes a photo the record does not mention, or if the record names a page that has dropped it. That is what makes withdrawal mean everywhere: delete the entry and the tool refuses to run until the photo is off every page, instead of leaving one behind.
